chem-phys-01-c1.text: Paul Flowers, Klaus Theopold, Richard Langley, William R. Robinson (2019). Chemistry 2e, 16.3 The Second and Third Laws of Thermodynamics. OpenStax, Rice University.
chem-phys-01-c1.quote: the entropy of a pure, perfect crystalline substance at 0 K is zero.
chem-phys-01-c1.claim: The third law says the entropy of a perfect crystal at 0 K is zero

chem-phys-01-c2.text: Paul Flowers, Klaus Theopold, Richard Langley, William R. Robinson (2019). Chemistry 2e, 5.3 Enthalpy. OpenStax, Rice University.
chem-phys-01-c2.quote: Enthalpy changes depend only on where a chemical process starts and ends, but not on the path it takes from start to finish.
chem-phys-01-c2.claim: Hess's law says enthalpy is a state function, so ΔH for a reaction is the same whatever path you take.

chem-phys-01-c2.text: Paul Flowers, Klaus Theopold, Richard Langley, William R. Robinson (2019). Chemistry 2e, 5.3 Enthalpy. OpenStax, Rice University.
chem-phys-01-c2.quote: the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable form is equal to zero under standard conditions
chem-phys-01-c2.claim: For the elements themselves in standard states, ΔH°_f = 0 by definition.
